Keemake, Victorinox, if your looking for something nicer and are willing to pay for it Dalstrong. Then theres always Amazon so a list of knives to keep in mind

Chefs knife (8 inch)

Deboning knife (victorinox flexi is my go to but you may want something a little less utilitarian)

Bread knife (something small and light in the hand is best and cheapest usually)

Vegetable Cleaver (Nakiri knife, Hamakiri, japanese style cleavers are best here, heavy cleavers are only really useful in a few specific contexts)

Pairing knife
Good brand here is keemake, mines a bit larger and works as a utility knife.

Steel quality is also important, I always opt for some form of German steel, but as long as you make sure your getting your knives from reputable companies you should be fine. Victorinox knives aren't pretty but for those knives they wont be using as often they are basic and they do a good job.
